# Components, Hooks & Storybook

Everything about designing, structuring, and presenting a React component or hook in this
project. Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting
rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic
numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS
conventions live in [css.md](./css.md).

---

## Components

- **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`).
  No default exports of anonymous functions.
- **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`,
  `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`.
- **Props type placement:**
  - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file.
  - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling
    files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with
    other shared types worth co-locating.
  - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone.
- **JSDoc** is required on:

  - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in
    [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)).
  - Any exported hook.
  - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour.

  Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient.

- **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`).
- **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions
  for "I forgot to mark it optional."
- **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get
  these right at authoring time:**
  - Every `<img>` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images).
  - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs
    an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to
    announce.
  - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`,
    `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role`
    attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an
    `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which
    is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour).

---

## Composition — writing a "clean" component

Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline
state belongs in a custom hook instead.

- **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and
  avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent
  paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced**
  — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so
  treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not
  something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding
  those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new
  dependency needed).
- **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/`
  receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like
  `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`
  / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container
  component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing
  "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just
  commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own
  data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched,
  mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it).

  **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may
  be called from any component, including presentational leaves. Both read from a Provider
  mounted above the route tree, not from a per-page/per-component fetch — so calling one from
  a leaf doesn't create the SSR/Storybook/parent-composition problem the rule above exists to
  prevent, and doesn't multiply fetches the way an SDK hook would. `useUiCopy`
  (`overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`, Provider at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/`)
  is the reference example — `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection` both call it directly
  for microcopy while still receiving their actual business data as props. This exception is
  narrow: it covers content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context,
  not anything that varies per page.

  **Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests and stories.** `useUiCopy`
  degrades to fallback text — `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY` — so a leaf calling
  it renders with zero setup. `useIntl` **throws** (`react-intl`'s `invariantIntlContext`:
  _"Could not find required `intl` object"_), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the **base
  SFCC `_app`**, not by `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. `.storybook/preview.tsx`
  supplies one for stories precisely because of this; any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl`
  consumer must wrap it too. An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed both hooks degrade
  gracefully and that both Providers sit in `_app-config`; neither is true of `useIntl`.
- **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook
  (`overrides/app/hooks/use<ComponentName><Feature>.ts`) when either is true:

  - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal
    the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer).
  - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial
    meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a
    one-line side effect.

  This one is judgment-heavy, not a hard mechanical gate — `/code-quality` should flag it as
  a should-fix, not a must-fix, and a component with ≥4 `useState` calls is a reasonable
  coarse trigger to at least stop and ask "should this be a hook?"

---

## Hooks

- **File extension** is `.ts` (no JSX in a hook file).
- **Exported function name** matches the filename: `useWishlist.ts` exports `useWishlist`.
- **Parameters and return value are typed** — no implicit `any`, no missing return type.
  See [typescript.md](./typescript.md) for the general typing rules this extends.
- **JSDoc** is required on every exported hook, including a `@returns` description.

---

## Storybook

Storybook is the canonical place to view components in isolation. Keep it browsable —
a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable.

### When a story is required

- **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/`
  or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports).
- **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent
  (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). Cover their
  variants via the parent's stories.
- Pages get a story showing the full assembly with representative props — not a story per
  sub-section.

### Categorisation

Story `title` drives the sidebar tree. Pick the first matching category:

| Category      | What goes here                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons, Shadows                                                                                                                                         |
| `Elements/`   | Generic building blocks — both display (Badge, Tag, Link, Avatar, Skeleton) and interactive controls (Button, Input, Checkbox, Select). Tiebreaker: _can it be used outside a form?_ → `Elements/`. |
| `Layout/`     | Global chrome, navigation, and structural components — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, ListMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Seo                                                                            |
| `Commerce/`   | Commerce-specific shared components — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup                                                                                               |
| `Forms/`      | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, CheckoutContactForm, NewsletterSignup                                                                                                                       |
| `Pages/`      | Full page assemblies — PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout, Account                                                                                                                                            |
| `Contentful/` | CMS-driven components — HeroBanner, RichText, ContentBlock. Use mock Contentful data in stories so variants are visible without a live CMS connection.                                              |

Naming convention: singular for a concept or proper noun (`Foundation`, `Commerce`, `Layout`, `Contentful`); plural for a collection (`Elements`, `Forms`, `Pages`).

Examples:

```ts
export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅
export default { title: 'Layout/Header' }; // ✅
export default { title: 'Elements/Button' }; // ✅
export default { title: 'Pages/PDP' }; // ✅
export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ — eCommerce specific, use Commerce/
export default { title: 'Primitives/Button' }; // ❌ — use Elements/
```

When in doubt: ask "what does this component _know_ about?" Commerce → `Commerce/`,
CMS-driven → `Contentful/`, nothing domain-specific → `Elements/`, page-level composition → `Pages/`.

### Story content

- Every story file has a `Default` named export.
- Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not
  for every possible prop combination.
- `play` functions only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting; otherwise the
  story is purely visual.

# Tagging & Environment Promotion

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. The **tag-promoted** tiers
(`test` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`) deploy a specific tag — never "whatever's on a branch right
now." (The continuous tiers are the exception: `dev` and `sit` deploy commit refs, and Test also
takes a branch ref for on-demand quick looks — see the Environment model below.)

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — it counts
  candidate builds, not deployments. The same `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be deployed (and re-deployed) to
  Test on demand; which environment ran which candidate is tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions
  run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull --ff-only   # fail rather than tag a local merge commit
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up through `uat` → `staging` → `prod`. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback.** The downgrade guard (see below) deliberately blocks deploying an older tag, so a
rollback takes one of two authorised paths:

- **Emergency (fastest) — re-activate the previous bundle in Managed Runtime**, outside the deploy
  pipeline (the rollback procedure in the Environment Topology doc). This does not run the guard, so
  afterwards re-record the baseline so it doesn't treat a superseded tag as live:
  `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record prod v0.1.0`.
- **Controlled — pipeline rollback with the guard override.** Redeploy the known-good tag with
  `rollback=true`; the guard's downgrade check is skipped (the run logs the skip for audit) and
  `record` still runs, so the rolled-back tag becomes the new live baseline:
  `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.1.0 -f rollback=true`. Because this bypasses the guard,
  its only human gate is the environment's **required reviewers** — so `prod` (and `staging`/`uat`)
  must have required reviewers with "prevent self-review" configured. **Prerequisite: until that is
  set, `rollback=true` is not gated.**

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

---

# Testing Conventions

Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.

**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
below for single-parent internal components still applies there.

| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |

> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.

---

## What to test (and what to skip)

Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:

- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches

---

## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)

### File layout

Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:

```
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
```

Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).

### Structure

- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.

### Mocking

- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
- **Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel
  (`app/components/icons`), which has a top-level side effect (`AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...`)
  that fails here because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings in this environment, not
  components. Not fixable from a test file — the SVG transform lives in `vitest.config.ts`,
  Tier 1 test config (AGENTS.md Hard Rule 8). Work around it by mocking `ZimmIcon` at the
  smallest surface in any test that renders an icon-consuming component:
  `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` — or,
  if an assertion depends on an accessible name the real `ZimmIcon` would carry (e.g. a
  fallback `<span aria-label>` with no wrapping interactive element), forward the relevant
  props instead of returning `null`. See `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` and
  `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for both variants.

### Commerce SDK hooks

Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks

---

## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)

### When to use `play`

Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:

- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
- Focus moves correctly through a flow
- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output

If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.

### Pattern

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'

export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
    }
}
```

- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.
- **Exception — Portal-rendered dialogs (Modal, Drawer).** Chakra's `Modal`/`Drawer` render their
  content via a React Portal that appends directly to `document.body`, outside `canvasElement` —
  and this project's `.storybook/preview.tsx` configures no custom portal container, so there is
  no way to reach that content through `within(canvasElement)`. A `play` function asserting on a
  portaled dialog's content queries `within(document.body)` instead for that assertion, with an
  inline comment citing this exception (see `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`'s `Large` story). This
  is the only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)` at this layer — every other query still
  goes through `within(canvasElement)`.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright

---

## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)

### Workflow

E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):

1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved

This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."

### File layout

```
e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
e2e/support/
  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
```

Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.

### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)

`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:

- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
  area's allow-list**. A single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
  claimed yet) resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` instead — `e2e-localhost` does not run at all on
  that PR (changed 2026-08-25, at the developer's request; previously fell back to running the
  full suite on every such PR). `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact
  path lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
- **This is a deliberate coverage trade-off, not a gap to silently work around.** A
  `develop`-targeted PR that can't be scoped to one area gets no PR-time E2E run at all — only
  unit tests / Storybook, plus BrowserStack if the PR references a Jira key with a tagged spec.
  Full/non-P0 regression coverage for that PR is deferred to the existing post-merge P0 gates
  (`deploy-test.yml`'s Test-tier gate, `digital-sit.yml`'s `playwright-p0` on `release/**`) —
  which only cover P0-tagged journeys, a subset of the full suite. A non-P0 regression introduced
  by a shared/global-path change can therefore reach `develop` before anything catches it. This
  was accepted deliberately to stop the full suite running on every PR touching a shared path
  (the single largest line item in this repo's CI-minutes usage) — revisit if it causes real
  regressions to slip through in practice.
- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff, unchanged — a release
  PR aggregates a whole sprint and gets the supervised, thorough pre-merge treatment per
  [releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md). This skip-instead-of-full
  behavior only applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage silently — it just means that
  spec's PRs get `e2e_scope: skip` (no PR-time run) instead of the scoping optimisation, same as
  any other unclaimed path.

### BrowserStack story scoping

`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
below for why):

- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).

Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.

**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.

**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.

**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a
Zephyr-tagged spec, and miss the build lookup entirely until the PR merges. An earlier version of
this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that
job DID run and the artifact is still missing, the sync job fails loudly instead of guessing a
fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
correctly, 2026-08-25).

**Desktop/mobile project isolation — a real gotcha, not a style choice.** BrowserStack Test
Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11
real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles showed
`passed: 0, skipped: 11` via BrowserStack's own API, not just the dashboard UI). `test.skip()`
does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and still clobbers.

The only real fix is to stop the "wrong" project from ever collecting that test at all, which
`playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already supports: the `chromium`
project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
regardless of what its title says.

**Access-gated preview URLs.** `BasePage.goto()` supports two optional env vars,
`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
the one real case this repo has needed so far.

**What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against.** Not the static `test` tier by default —
`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code.

**No fallback to the static test tier when that artifact is missing (removed 2026-08-26,
CodeRabbit flagged this correctly)** — an earlier version of this job silently fell back to the
static `test`-tier `RETAIL_APP_HOME` whenever `deploy-preview.yml` failed or hadn't finished. That
let a develop PR whose own deployment genuinely failed still produce a green, story-tagged Zephyr
execution (and a possible auto-filed Jira defect) that proved nothing about the PR's own code —
the exact condition the fallback existed to tolerate was the one that made its result meaningless.
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s "Resolve BrowserStack test target" step now fails the job loudly
(`::error::` + `exit 1`) instead when the hostname artifact is missing, whether that's because
Deploy Preview failed outright or succeeded but didn't reach the artifact-upload step. Same
principle [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)'s Graceful Degradation section already states for
checkout/payment: never silently substitute a different flow, surface an explicit error instead.
A cancelled Deploy Preview run is the one case with nothing to fail loudly about — the job-level
`if:` skips the whole job entirely rather than running it just to hit this failure, since there's
no meaningful error to surface for a run nobody asked to complete.

**This used to be a single job in `qa.yml` that polled for `deploy-preview.yml`'s run to finish —
that design is gone, not just retuned (2026-08-25 cost review).** It started alongside `Deploy
Preview` (both triggered by the same push) and slept in a loop waiting for it, since there was no
other way for one already-running, already-billed job to wait on a *different* workflow's run —
up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time per push, worst case, before the real BrowserStack run
even started. (An earlier version of this note described tuning that wait down from a wrongly
inflated 70-minute job timeout / 40-minute poll to 40/15 — that tuning is now moot; the wait
itself no longer exists.) `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` fixes this at the root by being a
separate workflow, `workflow_run`-triggered off `Deploy Preview`'s completion: GitHub fires it
the instant that run finishes, with the run ID and conclusion already in the event payload — no
polling, so no billed wait, ever. `release/**` PRs were never part of this problem —
`deploy-preview.yml` never runs for `fix/release-*` branches, so `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack`
job (which still handles that path) goes straight to the static test tier with nothing to wait
for.

- **`release/**`-targeted PRs (`qa.yml`):** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped.
  A release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
- **`develop`-targeted PRs (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`):** on `Deploy Preview`'s completion,
  the job finds the open PR for that branch (`gh pr list --head`, one call, no loop) and regexes
  `SFCC-\d+` out of its title, body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app
  uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own (duplicated from
  `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` step rather than shared — the two workflows have no other runtime
  dependency on each other). If at least one key is found, the job runs `--grep`-scoped to that
  story's tag(s) (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job exits
  without running BrowserStack.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results
  to in Zephyr, there's nothing correct to run. It also re-checks `qa.yml`'s own `e2e`-path
  relevance gate before running — a single non-looping artifact download from that commit's `QA`
  run — **but this is a fail-open check, not an unconditional guarantee** (CodeRabbit flagged the
  distinction correctly, 2026-08-26): the normal path is that a Jira-tagged PR touching nothing
  e2e-relevant genuinely skips BrowserStack. If the QA-run lookup or the `e2e-scope` artifact
  download itself fails for any reason (the run isn't found yet, the artifact expired, an API
  hiccup), this step assumes relevant rather than adding a retry loop to chase the optimisation —
  so in that specific failure case, a Jira-tagged PR can still run BrowserStack even when its
  changes weren't e2e-relevant. Worst case is one avoidable BrowserStack run, not a correctness
  problem, but it's a real exception to the "doesn't pay for a BrowserStack run" claim, not a
  universal guarantee.
- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
  by `e2e-localhost`.
- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.

### Multi-region fixtures

Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.

```ts
test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
    for (const site of SITES) {
        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
    }
})
```

### Page Object Model

Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:

1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).

Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Pure logic — that's Vitest
- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.

resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that

# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

**Report in "ELI5BITFEDLOTP" register** — Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The
Project. Not dumbed down, but no jargon in the way: consequence first, then mechanism, then fix.
Marcel reads your report as often as the skill that called you does.

**Scale to the work.** The plan states the scale it chose — honour it, and do not quietly
restore machinery it dropped. Over-scaled effort is a defect, not thoroughness. Two hard stops:
**never re-run an angle or a check against a diff that has not changed since you last ran it**,
and never re-present a conclusion that has not changed. Both have happened here — one session
re-ran an identical four-angle wave ninety minutes later with no commits in between, then ran a
further wave to validate that one.

## Two modes

**Build mode (default).** You are the gate on a Zimmermann build loop — score the work against the
six axes below and return PASS or REWORK. Everything in this file describes this mode.

**Findings mode.** `zimmerMANNReview` invokes you to score *claims* rather than work: does each
finding survive scrutiny? Return **CONFIRMED** (reproduced from source), **PLAUSIBLE** (consistent
with what you read, decisive evidence missing — say what would settle it), or **UNSUPPORTED** (the
citation does not support the claim — say what is actually true). The six axes do not apply.
Review supplies the full brief; this note exists so the mode is not a surprise to anyone reading
this file.

The rest of this file is **build mode.**

---

You see the plan step, the diff, the Tester's findings and the Orchestrator's scope verdict, and
you decide whether the work is done.

You are independent of the builder and the tester. You are not a cheerleader and you are not a
second tester. Your job is a **judgement**: is this good enough to move on, given what the step
said it would deliver?

## The six axes

| Axis | What PASS looks like |
|---|---|
| **Pass criteria** | Every criterion in the step is met, with evidence — not asserted |
| **Correctness** | `tsc` clean, `npm run test` green, no 🔴 findings from the Tester |
| **Design fidelity** | The rendered output matches the named Figma nodes — variants, states, spacing, tokens |
| **Conformance** | Styling hierarchy, recipe namespacing, structure and import rules all hold |
| **Completeness** | Story and test present where the rules require them; ACs actually satisfied |
| **Restraint** | Nothing built — and nothing re-run — that the step didn't ask for |

**Design fidelity is its own axis and cannot be inferred from green gates.** No automated check on
this stack catches a layout defect: `width: 'xl'` resolved through `theme.sizes`, blew contact
icons to 576px and destroyed the global footer on every page — while passing tsc, eslint, vitest,
CodeRabbit and Storybook a11y. If the visual checkpoint has not happened yet for a step that
changes rendered output, this axis is **UNVERIFIED**, not PASS.

**Restraint takes its evidence from the Orchestrator's verdict.** An OVER or UNDER verdict fails
this axis; you make the judgement, the Orchestrator supplies the finding.

**Restraint covers effort as well as output.** "Nothing built that the step didn't ask for" and
"nothing *run* that the step didn't warrant" are the same axis. Take the code half from the
Orchestrator; take the effort half from the Tester's scale line — angles run against angles the
plan allowed. An unexplained over-run fails Restraint exactly as unasked-for code does, because
the expensive failure on this project has been re-running work that had not changed, not writing
too much of it.

## Verdict

**PASS** — all six hold. **REWORK** — one or more fail.

On REWORK, say exactly which axis, quote the evidence, and give the Implementer a specific
instruction. "Improve quality" is not an instruction; "`footer.css.ts:22` uses `gap: 'xs'` — a bare
token key that fails recipeGuards guard 4; use `var(--zimm-scale-xs)`" is.

Label each finding **CONFIRMED** or **PLAUSIBLE**.

## Two required sections

**What I tried to falsify.** A PASS with no falsification attempt is not a PASS. Say what you
attacked and how the work survived. A verification pass that finds nothing has not been shown to
be capable of finding anything.

**What I could not verify.** Name what you could not reach, and say plainly if an axis is
UNVERIFIED rather than passed.

## Output shape

1. Per-axis table, six rows, most severe first
2. **Overall: PASS or REWORK**
3. What I tried to falsify
4. What I could not verify
5. Each defect: `file:line`, severity, CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE, and the specific instruction
6. If PASS: the single biggest residual risk in shipping this step

## The round cap

Track the round number. **On the third REWORK for the same step, stop the loop** and surface to
Marcel with what has been tried, what is still failing, and your read on why it isn't converging.
Three failed rounds means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not the implementation.

Never soften a verdict to end the loop, and never soften one to be agreeable. A false PASS moves
the defect downstream to CodeRabbit, to Tim, or to production.

---

180	#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)
181	
182	**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.
183	
184	**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.
185	
186	**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.
187	
188	**Pass criteria.**
189	1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
190	2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
191	3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
192	4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

314	1. With `isOnSale` and a `listPrice`, the struck "Was" and the "Now" both render, and both scale with quantity.

319	
320	**Changes.** `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartItemMapper.ts` converts an SDK basket `productItem` to the override's props — the `productListCardMapper.ts` precedent from PR #85. This is what keeps every component in B3 prop-driven with no data-fetching hook in a leaf. `useIntl` is permitted in leaves (Context-backed exception); nothing else is.

324	**Pass criteria.**

331

Same root cause, same discovery: `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4, commit `f2612b92`) is not plumbed into the real stepper either — no `max` is ever passed to the real, currently-rendered component, so there is no live cap enforcement anywhere today. Marcel's call (2026-09-18): plan both wirings in now rather than leave them standalone indefinitely.
333	
334	**Changes.** In `product-item/index.tsx`, replace the `ProductQuantityPicker` branch (the `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity` is a separate, static display for free/bonus items and is out of this step's scope) with `ZimmQuantityStepper`. `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component (`quantity`/`min`/`max`/`isUnavailable`/`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`) — a different contract than `ProductQuantityPicker`'s `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split, so this is real integration, not a prop rename. Keep `product-item`'s own existing `quantity`/`setQuantity` local state; wire `onDecrement`/`onIncrement` to call the same `onItemQuantityChange`-then-conditionally-`setQuantity` flow the old `handleQuantityChange` used, adapted to the new callback shape (each receives the already-computed next value directly, unlike the old picker's raw string/number input-change event).

337	
338	`isUnavailable` — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already established as out of this whole epic's scope). Leave unset/`false` for this step, same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle step 3.2 already established for `message`. Do not invent a detection heuristic.
339	
340	**Pass criteria.**
341	1. `product-item/index.test.tsx`: with `product.c_maxOrderQuantity` absent, the rendered stepper's effective max resolves to 3 (the util's own fallback) — assert via the real DOM (e.g. clicking `+` from quantity 3 does nothing further, or the increment control's `aria-disabled` state at that boundary), not by asserting the util was called with the right arguments alone.
342	2. With `c_maxOrderQuantity: 5` on the product, the stepper allows incrementing up to 5 and no further.
343	3. At quantity 1, decrement is disabled (matches `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own step-3.1 tested contract, resolves the audit's floor-of-0-vs-1 finding).
344	4. `BonusProductQuantity`'s own render branch and props are unchanged — diff `product-item/index.tsx` and confirm nothing in that branch moved.
345	5. `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own existing test suite (step 3.1) still passes unmodified — this step wires an existing, already-tested component, it does not change its own contract.
346	6. Storybook: `product-item/index.stories.tsx`'s existing stories all still render without throwing (the swapped-in stepper needs `min`/`max`/`onDecrement`/`onIncrement`, confirm every existing story still supplies enough for it to render, adding args where a story genuinely needs them).
347	
348	#### Step 3.6 — Accessibility sweep against 795's 11 a11y ACs (renumbered from 3.5, 2026-09-18 — step 3.5 above now owns the stepper-wiring gap this sweep originally found)
349	
350	**Changes.** Mostly verification — the 11 accessibility ACs are each checked off explicitly, now against the *real*, newly-wired stepper from step 3.5, not the orphaned `ZimmQuantityStepper` story in isolation. One real fix included: `ZimmInlineMessage` is not programmatically associated with its line item today (DOM adjacency only, no explicit ARIA link) — Marcel's call (2026-09-18): cheap, fix it now as part of going through this checklist. Give the rendered message element a real `id` and reference it via `aria-describedby` on the quantity control it's describing (the message is about the item's quantity/availability state, which is what the stepper controls) — exact mechanism left to the implementer, following whatever pattern other associated-error-text components in this codebase (form field + validation message, if any exist) already use, or a straightforward `aria-describedby` pairing if none do.
351	
352	**Pass criteria.** One checkable line per AC, enumerated in the PR body, each naming the file and the assertion that proves it. At minimum: every `IconButton` has `aria-label`; every `<img>` has `alt`; quantity changes announce via a live region (base `product-quantity-picker` already ships a `VisuallyHidden role="status"` — preserve it, do not delete it in the restyle; **known pre-existing defect, confirmed unmodified base SFCC behaviour, out of this step's own scope to fix**: the announcement reads the static `product.quantity` prop, not the live interactive value, so it never actually updates — flagged, not silently left undocumented); stepper controls reachable and operable by keyboard alone (now against the real `ZimmQuantityStepper`); focus-visible ring present and distinguishable on stepper, both action links (**`ZimmCartItemActions`/step 4.4 doesn't exist yet — unverifiable until then, not a failure of this step**), and the drawer close; the inline message is programmatically associated with its line item (**the one real fix this step makes — was a genuine gap, not just an audit false-negative**); target sizes ≥24px; no colour-only state conveyance. Storybook a11y check green on every story in B3.
353	
354	**Known, disclosed, NOT fixed in this step (Tier 1 / cross-cutting, needs UI-designer sign-off, not this build's authority to resolve):** `text.muted` (`grey[300]`, `#969696`) fails WCAG AA contrast against white at the sizes this build renders it (measured 2.95:1, needs 4.5:1) — confirmed via the real Storybook a11y test-runner, not assumed. This is not new to this step or this epic: `colour.ts`'s own existing comment already flags `grey[300]` as an unresolved Handover self-contradiction (`#969696` vs `#939393` — checked: the alternate value doesn't fix the contrast problem either, both are too light). The same token is already shipped in 10+ other components across the storefront (footer, product card, product price, size chip, button, subscribe modal, icons) — this may already be a live accessibility issue outside this epic entirely, not something this step introduced. Ship to the current spec value per this repo's own established precedent for exactly this situation (`colour.ts`'s own "shipping the current value, confirm with the UI designer" comment) — raise with the UI designer post-build, do not silently drop it and do not invent a replacement value unilaterally.

Both inputs read in full, plus the path/tier checks needed to make the manifest real. Four things I found change the plan's shape — flagged inline where they land.

---

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, 18 commits.**
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, owners read directly from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`. Not from `.claude/registry/*.md`.

### B0 — e2e area

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/qa.yml` | modify | **Tier 1 CI/CD** | `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` |

> **BLOCKED.** Named explicitly in the brief, but owner approval is not confirmed. ### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

schema.name: Bash
schema.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.

  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
