Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it

import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';

/**
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute — a real BM site preference
 * (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto the SCAPI product response via a
 * `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (406913046). It has no
 * typed field on the base SDK's `Product` type — it only reaches this shape via that type's own
 * `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, the same situation
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` lines 16-23 document for a
 * different custom attribute (`c_productBadges`). Narrowed here to a local type rather than
 * trusting `any` at the call site, per AGENTS.md's Gotchas: "Commerce SDK types not importable
 * ... declare a narrow local type."
 *
 * Typed `unknown`, not `number | undefined`: this function's whole job is validating a value
 * that may legitimately arrive absent, as `0`, negative, or non-numeric (see the pass criteria
 * this file's own test covers) — typing it as `number | undefined` would assert a guarantee the
 * real BM data doesn't have.
 *
 * As of this commit `TSD-SFCC-268` is still `v0.1 Draft` (Technical Lead sign-off Pending) and a
 * live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the `afterGET` hook is
 * not deployed yet. Reading the field with the fallback below degrades to today's hardcoded
 * behaviour while that remains true, and picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships,
 * with no further frontend change needed.
 */
type ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
  c_maxOrderQuantity?: unknown;
};

/**
 * Frontend fallback when no valid `c_maxOrderQuantity` is present. Matches
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s own `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` value (3) exactly
 * (see that file's lines 124-125: "Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform
 * max-order-quantity field."), but is deliberately its own, independent constant rather than a
 * shared/promoted one — the TSD's resolution order is product override (SFCC-703) -> site
 * preference -> this hardcoded value, so a constant shared between the PDP and this cart-facing
 * util would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway.
 */
const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;

/**
 * Reads the real per-product order-quantity cap off a SCAPI product response
 * (`c_maxOrderQuantity`), falling back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` when the attribute is
 * absent or not a valid, usable cap (zero, negative, or non-numeric) — see this file's own
 * module docblock for why a shared constant is deliberately not used here.
 *
 * @param product A SCAPI product response (or product-shaped object) that may carry
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity`.
 * @returns The product's real max order quantity, or `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` (3) when no
 * valid value is present.
 */
export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
  const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
};

64	 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,

109	 * `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity`'s own branch is untouched)

112	 * step 3.4) and `min={1}` — this component's own tested floor since step 3.1, superseding the old
113	 * picker's floor of 0, which was never actually speced or tested against any AC.
114	 * `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component with a different callback contract
115	 * (`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`, receiving the already-computed next
116	 * value directly) than the old picker's `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split (which parsed
117	 * a raw input-change event) — `handleStepperQuantityChange` below is the adapter between the two,
118	 * and it preserves the old `handleQuantityChange`'s real-mutation-then-conditionally-update-
119	 * local-state flow exactly: call `onItemQuantityChange` first, only commit the new quantity to

124	 * step's own instruction not to delete a file unasked. `isUnavailable` is left unset on the new

130	import React from 'react';
131	
132	// Chakra Components
133	import {
134	  Box,
135	  Fade,
136	  Flex,
137	  Stack,
138	  Text,
139	  useMultiStyleConfig,
140	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
141	
142	// Project Components
143	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
144	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
145	import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
146	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
147	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
148	import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
149	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
150	import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
151	import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
152	import { ZimmQuantityStepper } from 'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper';
153	
154	// Hooks
155	import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';
156	
157	// Utils
158	import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';
159	
160	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
161	
162	type SfccProduct = any;
163	
164	type ProductItemProps = {
165	  product: SfccProduct;
166	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
167	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
168	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
169	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
170	  /**
171	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
172	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
173	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
174	   */
175	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
176	  showLoading?: boolean;
177	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
178	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
179	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
180	  isRemoving?: boolean;
181	  pickupInStore?: boolean;
182	  /**
183	   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
184	   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
185	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
186	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
187	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
188	   */
189	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
190	  /**
191	   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
192	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
193	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
194	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
195	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
196	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
197	   */
198	  message?: {
199	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
200	    text: string;
201	  };
202	  /**
203	   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
204	   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
205	   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
206	   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
207	   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
208	   *
209	   * Styling: rendered via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, not a bespoke element —
210	   * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node, superseding
211	   * the prior, wrong precedent this JSDoc used to cite). The pulled node is `color:
212	   * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
213	   * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption",
214	   * byte-identical to this codebase's own `status.success` token (green[500] = '#2d5a3d',
215	   * theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80, registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success) in
216	   * zimmTokens.ts:73) and the exact same node family `ZimmInlineMessage`'s `error`/`warning`
217	   * variants already render (regular weight, 12px/18px — see that component's own docblock). The
218	   * previous version of this comment cited item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part as "the
219	   * nearest existing sibling treatment" and stated no Figma node existed for this element — both
220	   * wrong: `colourSize` is a DIFFERENT, MEDIUM-weight node ("Default/Caption-strong", the "Lilac
221	   * Sand, One size" line), and a real node did exist, just not yet pulled. Confirmed directly
222	   * with Marcel: no icon on this variant (matching `error`'s own no-icon behaviour, unlike
223	   * `warning`).
224	   */
225	  discountLabel?: string;
226	};
227	
228	/**
229	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
230	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
231	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
232	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
233	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
234	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
235	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
236	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
237	 */
238	const ProductItem = ({
239	  product,
240	  primaryAction,
241	  secondaryActions,
242	  deliveryActions,
243	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
244	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
245	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
246	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
247	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
248	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
249	  showLoading = false,
250	  containerStyles = {},
251	  isRemoving = false,
252	  pickupInStore = false,
253	  hideStepperAndActions = false,
254	  message,
255	  discountLabel,
256	}: ProductItemProps) => {
257	  const { showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
258	    product,
259	    false,
260	    false,
261	    pickupInStore,
262	  );
263	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
264	  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
265	  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
266	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
267	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
268	  // SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5): shared by both ZimmQuantityStepper callbacks below — see this
269	  // file's own docblock for why this exact call order (real mutation first, conditional local
270	  // commit second) is load-bearing, not incidental.
271	  const handleStepperQuantityChange = (nextQuantity: number) => {
272	    void Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(
273	      (isValidChange: boolean) => isValidChange && setQuantity(nextQuantity),
274	    );
275	  };
276	  return (
277	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
278	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
279	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
280	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
281	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
282	            <CartItemVariantImage />
283	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
284	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
285	                <Stack spacing={1}>
286	                  <CartItemVariantName />
287	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
288	                  <HideOnDesktop>
289	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
290	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
291	                    </Box>
292	                  </HideOnDesktop>
293	                </Stack>
294	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
295	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
296	                )}
297	              </Flex>
298	
299	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
300	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
301	              )}
302	
303	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
304	                <Stack spacing={1}>
305	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
306	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
307	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
308	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
309	                    ) : (
310	                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
311	                        quantity={quantity}
312	                        min={1}
313	                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
314	                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
315	                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
316	                      />
317	                    ))}
318	                </Stack>
319	                <Stack>
320	                  <HideOnMobile>
321	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
322	                  </HideOnMobile>
323	                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
324	                </Stack>
325	              </Flex>
326	
327	              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
328	                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
329	                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
330	              {discountLabel && (
331	                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
332	              )}
333	
334	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
335	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
336	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
337	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
338	
339	              <Box>
340	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
341	                  <Fade in={true}>
342	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
343	                      {inventoryMessage}
344	                    </Text>
345	                  </Fade>
346	                )}
347	              </Box>
348	
349	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
350	            </Stack>
351	          </Flex>
352	
353	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
354	            <HideOnDesktop>
355	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
356	            </HideOnDesktop>
357	          )}
358	        </Stack>
359	      </ItemVariantProvider>
360	    </Box>
361	  );
362	};
363	
364	export default ProductItem;

 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
 *
 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): `discountLabel` (optional, prop-driven) renders directly beneath the
 * stepper/price row: DOM order is stepper -> discountLabel -> message -> secondaryActions.
 * "Beneath the stepper" is sourced (session-notes.md line 394's own ticket-summary prose, and the
 * plan's own step 3.3 pass criterion 2 wording); placing it AHEAD of `message` specifically is
 * this component's own disclosed interpretation, not a directly sourced requirement — no citation
 * in session-notes.md sequences discountLabel relative to message (checked directly, not assumed),
 * and the pass criterion itself is satisfied by "beneath the stepper" alone regardless of order.
 * Chosen because a discount is a property of the line item's own state (always true or false for
 * that line), while `message` is closer to point-of-action feedback nearer the actions row — a
 * reasonable read, not a tested one. Revisit if a future Figma pull sources the real order.
 * Purely presentational, per session-notes.md §4's SFCC-795 decisions
 * ("Only the discount label is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired
 * when the promotions engine lands"): this component does not compute a discount percentage or
 * label itself; a caller supplies the already-resolved string once something upstream (the
 * promotions engine, and whatever cart-item mapper eventually feeds this component real basket
 * data) is wired — neither is built yet as of this commit. Undefined (every existing caller today)
 * renders nothing — no empty node is emitted. See the prop's own JSDoc below for the styling —
 * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node): a real Figma
 * citation exists now (this paragraph used to say none did, true only in the sense that none had
 * been pulled yet), and the label renders via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"` rather than
 * the bespoke, wrongly-precedented `<Text>` this component used to render directly.
 *
 * The was/now promotional-price mechanism itself (`ListPrice` struck "Was" beside the current
 * "Now", both quantity-scaled) is NOT new at this step and is not touched here — it already lives
 * in base `display-price` (rendered via item-variant/item-price.tsx, unmodified by this commit).
 * See this component's own test file for a disclosed, verified limitation on exactly where that
 * mechanism is and isn't reachable today.
 *
 * SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5, inserted 2026-09-18): the quantity-stepper branch below (the
 * `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity`'s own branch is untouched)
 * now renders `ZimmQuantityStepper` (built and tested at step 3.1) instead of base-styled
 * `ProductQuantityPicker`, with `max` sourced from `getMaxOrderQuantity` (built and tested at
 * step 3.4) and `min={1}` — this component's own tested floor since step 3.1, superseding the old
 * picker's floor of 0, which was never actually speced or tested against any AC.
 * `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component with a different callback contract
 * (`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`, receiving the already-computed next
 * value directly) than the old picker's `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split (which parsed
 * a raw input-change event) — `handleStepperQuantityChange` below is the adapter between the two,
 * and it preserves the old `handleQuantityChange`'s real-mutation-then-conditionally-update-
 * local-state flow exactly: call `onItemQuantityChange` first, only commit the new quantity to
 * local state via `setQuantity` if that call resolves truthy. Writing straight to `setQuantity`
 * instead (skipping the real mutation) would make the stepper look like it works while the real
 * basket on the server silently stops updating. `product-quantity-picker.tsx` itself is untouched
 * and, as of this commit, no longer imported anywhere in this file — left in place per this
 * step's own instruction not to delete a file unasked. `isUnavailable` is left unset on the new
 * stepper — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already out of
 * this epic's scope) — matching the same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle the
 * `message` prop above already establishes. Giving `ZimmInlineMessage` a real ARIA association
 * with this stepper is plan step 3.6, a later step not yet run as of this commit.
 */
import React from 'react';

// Chakra Components
import {
  Box,
  Fade,
  Flex,
  Stack,
  Text,
  useMultiStyleConfig,
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

// Project Components
import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
import { ZimmQuantityStepper } from 'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper';

// Hooks
import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';

// Utils
import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';

const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';

type SfccProduct = any;

type ProductItemProps = {
  product: SfccProduct;
  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
  /**
   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
   */
  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
  showLoading?: boolean;
  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
  isRemoving?: boolean;
  pickupInStore?: boolean;
  /**
   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
   */
  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
  /**
   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
   */
  message?: {
    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
    text: string;
  };
  /**
   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
   *
   * Styling: rendered via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, not a bespoke element —
   * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node, superseding
   * the prior, wrong precedent this JSDoc used to cite). The pulled node is `color:
   * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
   * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption",
   * byte-identical to this codebase's own `status.success` token (green[500] = '#2d5a3d',
   * theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80, registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success) in
   * zimmTokens.ts:73) and the exact same node family `ZimmInlineMessage`'s `error`/`warning`
   * variants already render (regular weight, 12px/18px — see that component's own docblock). The
   * previous version of this comment cited item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part as "the
   * nearest existing sibling treatment" and stated no Figma node existed for this element — both
   * wrong: `colourSize` is a DIFFERENT, MEDIUM-weight node ("Default/Caption-strong", the "Lilac
   * Sand, One size" line), and a real node did exist, just not yet pulled. Confirmed directly
   * with Marcel: no icon on this variant (matching `error`'s own no-icon behaviour, unlike
   * `warning`).
   */
  discountLabel?: string;
};

/**
 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
 */
const ProductItem = ({
  product,
  primaryAction,
  secondaryActions,
  deliveryActions,
  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
  showLoading = false,
  containerStyles = {},
  isRemoving = false,
  pickupInStore = false,
  hideStepperAndActions = false,
  message,
  discountLabel,
}: ProductItemProps) => {
  const { showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
    product,
    false,
    false,
    pickupInStore,
  );
  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
  // SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5): shared by both ZimmQuantityStepper callbacks below — see this
  // file's own docblock for why this exact call order (real mutation first, conditional local
  // commit second) is load-bearing, not incidental.
  const handleStepperQuantityChange = (nextQuantity: number) => {
    void Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(
      (isValidChange: boolean) => isValidChange && setQuantity(nextQuantity),
    );
  };
  return (
    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
            <CartItemVariantImage />
            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
                <Stack spacing={1}>
                  <CartItemVariantName />
                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
                  <HideOnDesktop>
                    <Box marginTop={2}>
                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
                    </Box>
                  </HideOnDesktop>
                </Stack>
                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
                )}
              </Flex>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
              )}

              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
                <Stack spacing={1}>
                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
                    ) : (
                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
                        quantity={quantity}
                        min={1}
                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                      />
                    ))}
                </Stack>
                <Stack>
                  <HideOnMobile>
                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
                  </HideOnMobile>
                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
                </Stack>
              </Flex>

              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
              {discountLabel && (
                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
              )}

              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}

              <Box>
                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
                  <Fade in={true}>
                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
                      {inventoryMessage}
                    </Text>
                  </Fade>
                )}
              </Box>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
            </Stack>
          </Flex>

          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
            <HideOnDesktop>
              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
            </HideOnDesktop>
          )}
        </Stack>
      </ItemVariantProvider>
    </Box>
  );
};

export default ProductItem;

1	/**
2	 * Commerce/ProductItem — Storybook stories for the cart line-item shell (SFCC-270, plan
3	 * step 2.2), restyled to the Figma cart-item spec.
4	 *
5	 * Providers supplied by .storybook/preview.tsx: IntlProvider, ChakraProvider.
6	 * This file adds its own inert provider stack, matching product-view/index.stories.tsx's own
7	 * documented pattern (see that file for the full rationale):
8	 *   MemoryRouter — item-name.tsx's <Link> (react-router-dom) and useMultiSite (via
9	 *     MultiSiteProvider below) both need Router/site context.
10	 *   MultiSiteProvider — useMultiSite (item-name.tsx's <Link>'s buildUrl, and
11	 *     StoreLocatorProvider below, which reads the current site to namespace its localStorage key).
12	 *   StoreLocatorProvider — `useDerivedProduct` (via item-price.tsx/item-attributes.tsx's own
13	 *     transitive dependency chain) unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`
14	 *     (`use-selected-store.js`), which throws `'useSelectedStore must be used within a
15	 *     StoreLocatorProvider'` with no Provider present — round 2 rework fix, confirmed by reading
16	 *     that hook's source, not assumed. Nested inside MultiSiteProvider (its own body calls
17	 *     useMultiSite()), outside CommerceProviders (its one consumer, `useSelectedStore`'s internal
18	 *     `useStores` call, resolves with `enabled: false` here since no story sets a selected store
19	 *     in localStorage, so it never actually needs Commerce context — but this file nests it
20	 *     inside CommerceProviders anyway for a single consistent provider order). `config={{}}` is a
21	 *     deliberately empty stand-in — no story here drives real store-locator state, so there is no
22	 *     real config value to supply; PropTypes will warn on the missing required fields, which is
23	 *     inert noise, not a render failure.
24	 *   CommerceApiProvider + QueryClientProvider — item-attributes.tsx's usePromotions/
25	 *     useProducts/useProduct/useCurrentBasket (via
26	 *     `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-basket`). `disableAuthInit` +
27	 *     an `.invalid` proxy URL prevent any real network calls; none of this story's mock line
28	 *     items carry priceAdjustments/bundledProductItems/type.bundle, so every one of those
29	 *     hooks resolves with `enabled: false` and never actually fetches.
30	 *   CurrencyProvider — useCurrency (item-price.tsx, product-item/index.tsx itself).
31	 *   ServerContext.Provider (from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`, not commerce-sdk-react) —
32	 *     found live in Storybook, not anticipated: item-attributes.tsx's useCurrentBasket() call
33	 *     above has its own separate transitive chain (useSFPayments -> useAppOrigin -> useOrigin)
34	 *     that calls the SDK's useServerContext() and destructures `res` from it unconditionally.
35	 *     With no Provider, useContext returns undefined and the destructure throws before useOrigin's
36	 *     own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res` at all) is reached.
37	 *     `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
38	 *     client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
39	 *
40	 * `GiftCard` story (round 2 rework): renders `ProductItem` with the new `hideStepperAndActions`
41	 * prop (SFCC-270 round 2, session-notes.md §11.2) set to true, on a plausible mock line item —
42	 * NOT a real gift-card detection, which this build still cannot do (see index.tsx's own docblock;
43	 * unchanged finding from the prior round). This story demonstrates the capability half only:
44	 * that when a caller explicitly asks to hide the stepper/actions, neither renders.
45	 */
46	import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
47	import { fn } from 'storybook/test';
48	import React from 'react';
49	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
50	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
51	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
52	import { CurrencyProvider, MultiSiteProvider, StoreLocatorProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts';
53	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
54	import ProductItem from '.';
55	
56	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	// Commerce provider stack (inert — no real API calls). See product-view/index.stories.tsx.
58	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	const storybookQueryClient = new QueryClient({
60	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
61	});
62	
63	const CommerceProviders = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
64	  <QueryClientProvider client={storybookQueryClient}>
65	    <CommerceApiProvider
66	      clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
67	      organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
68	      shortCode="storybook"
69	      siteId="ZimmermannAU"
70	      locale="en-AU"
71	      currency="AUD"
72	      proxy="https://storybook.invalid/mobify/proxy/api"
73	      redirectURI="https://storybook.invalid/callback"
74	      disableAuthInit
75	      silenceWarnings
76	    >
77	      <CurrencyProvider currency="AUD">{children}</CurrencyProvider>
78	    </CommerceApiProvider>
79	  </QueryClientProvider>
80	);

- Scoped `eslint` to just the 3 touched files, then used `git stash` to diff lint output before/after this step's changes — identical 3 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors, both times. - Ran `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` before/after via the same stash technique — identical "7 unacknowledged violation(s)," none in `product-item/` or `item-variant/`. This step adds zero new token findings, as the brief expected.
- Scoped-ran the two relevant suites directly (`npx vitest run .../zimmQuantityStepper/index.test.tsx .../product-item/index.test.tsx`) to get an exact per-file count rather than trusting the "17/17" claim — confirmed exactly 17/17 for the stepper (genuinely unmodified — not in `git status` at all) and 19/19 for product-item (10 pre-existing + 9 new, matching what the diff actually adds).
- Read the new "synchronous callback" test's own comment (`overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx:553-563`) claiming it closes a real mutation-blind gap, and checked the logic: the added `expect(onItemQuantityChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith(3)` genuinely would fail under the "wire onIncrement straight to setQuantity" shortcut the comment describes, since that shortcut never calls `onItemQuantityChange` at all. - I did not re-run the Tester's real-Chromium behavioural/a11y verification — already done rigorously against this unchanged diff; redoing it would be exactly the re-run this review is supposed to avoid.

None at CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE severity in the code itself. The one open item is procedural, not a code defect:

Instruction: get that look (Storybook `Commerce/ProductItem` or live surface) before this commits; see Fix above for the two specific things worth checking. No code change implied unless the look finds something.

Full-repo `npm run lint` is currently failing hard — 896 problems (mostly prettier formatting) across roughly 40 files, none of them touched by this step (confirmed via stash comparison, identical before/after this diff). This isn't news that lint doesn't gate CI here — that's already tracked — but the scale of drift is bigger than a "known gap" framing suggests, and it's compounding: worth a dedicated cleanup pass before it grows further or before lint ever becomes a required check.
